newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices ease in general slowdown.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices ease in general slowdown.

text.p: German wheat prices are easing because of a generally weaker global market and a lack of export opportunities, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Supply exceeds demand in most trading centres and farmers are more willing to sell than they have been for a long time," one said.
"Some wheat may have to end up in intervention."
British feed wheat import offers for March-June also featured, adding to local supply and helping to drag the bread wheat market lower.
The relatively low level of awards at last week's EU export tender also weighed on sentiment, as did news of Poland's plans to re-introduce 10 percent duties on most grain imports.
But exporters said previously agreed contracts would be carried out without tax and they were hopeful duties would be suspended again if Poland's internal prices rose rapidly.
They were also hoping for Russian and Uzbek interest.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week kept its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) free Hamburg at 275 marks a tonne and spot feed wheat at 272.50.
The January intervention buying-in price is 238.95 marks.

Top quality grain in the fob Baltic export market was marked down and average qualities were merely steady as the market moved into first half Feb. Sellers would normally have asked for storage increments.
Spot bread wheat (12 percent protein) for first half Feb was at 285-287.50 marks and 13 percent material at 290-295, but 14 percent qualities were down 2.50 marks at 300-302.50.
Domestic barley prices eased as local and Danish buyers took advantage of cheap feed wheat prices, but fob barley was broadly steady at 260-274 marks.
Fob rye offers were at 255-270, up from 254-268 previously.
